intent: Lay out tabular data as a styled native HTML table, rows that share the same columns.
typical_uses: Rows of records that share the same columns and are read down a column as well as across a row
The markup layer under sorting, filtering or paging logic the caller owns

dont_use_when.situation: Sorting, row selection and pagination that the component should own, from one columns/data pair
One record's key/value details or a summary panel
A list of similar entries that do not share columns (media, a title and a trailing action per row)

invariants.text: Table renders a scrolling div around the <table>: it scrolls horizontally when the table is wider than it, and vertically once it is given a height. `label`, `containerClassName` (merged after the wrapper's kit class) and `containerStyle` land on that wrapper. Every other prop apart from `density` and `variant` - className, style, aria attributes, event handlers - lands on the inner <table>.

The wrapper always carries tabIndex 0, whether or not the table overflows, so keyboard users can scroll it with the arrow keys. `label` gives the wrapper role="region" and an aria-label; without it the wrapper has no role and no name. `label` names the wrapper only - the table's own accessible name comes from TableCaption or from aria-label / aria-labelledby passed to Table.

`variant="collection"` switches the table to a fixed layout on a 960px minimum width, gives the header cells a taller band on the card fill, sets body rows to a 4rem height and lets cell text wrap. `density="compact"` lowers the header height and the cells' block padding and applies inside either variant; in the collection view the body rows keep their 4rem height.

anti_patterns.dont: Wrap Table in your own div and put role="region" and aria-label on that div
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `label` to Table - the focusable scroll wrapper is Table's own, and a name on an outer div lands on an element that never takes focus

anti_patterns.dont: Cap a long table through Table's style or through an outer div of your own
anti_patterns.do_instead: Put the max-height on Table's own scroll wrapper through `containerStyle` or `containerClassName`. `style` lands on the <table>, which does not scroll, and a sticky header sticks to its nearest scrolling ancestor, which is that wrapper; with the height on an outer div the wrapper never scrolls vertically, so the collection view's header scrolls away with the rows

a11y.by: table.test.tsx asserts getByRole('table') with three rows, two columnheaders and four cells under it, and that `label` exposes the wrapper as getByRole('region', { name: 'Quarterly results' })

containerStyle.states: containerStyle is a plain React style object applied to the scroll wrapper, not to the <table>
containerStyle.because: TableProps types it as React's `CSSProperties`; the compiler has no JSON type for `CSSProperties`, so nothing is asserted. The wrapper's own styling goes through table.module.css, not through this.

unexposed_parts.reason: Table renders a div around its <table> with overflow auto and tabIndex 0; it is not exported, and `label`, `containerClassName` and `containerStyle` are the only props that reach it.

good.title: A captioned table with a header, a body and a totals footer
A compact collection view with a named scroll region

bad.title: The region name put on an outer div
bad.why: The element that takes keyboard focus is Table's own wrapper inside this div, and it stays nameless; pass `label="Invoices"` to Table instead.
